prior_importants.description: `refuseUninstalled` refuses any nested package that declares dependencies but has no `node_modules` of its own in the main checkout. That includes npm and yarn-v1 workspace members whose dependencies are hoisted to the root `node_modules`. The gate links that root directory into the checkout (`linkEnvironment(..., '.')`), and those stages used to pass. Now every merge touching such a member is refused as an operator error, and the install command it suggests does not create a member `node_modules`.

findings.description: `resolvesAbove` accepts a dependency found in `node_modules` folders the gate checkout never gets. These are intermediate folders, and the root's for a package with its own lockfile. In those layouts the refusal is skipped and the stage fails on a missing runner, which reads as the branch's fault.
findings.body:
**`resolvesAbove` counts `node_modules` folders the gate never links.**

`resolvesAbove` walks every ancestor of `pkg.dir` in the main checkout:

```ts
for (let rel = dirname(dir); ; rel = dirname(rel)) {
  if (existsSync(join(repoPath, rel, GATE_ENVIRONMENT_DIR, dependency))) return true;
  if (rel === '.') return false;
}
```

`measureBranch` only links `'.'` and the touched packages' own folders (`for (const rel of ['.', ...nestedPackages.map((pkg) => pkg.dir)])`). The checkout lives in a temp `pup-gate-*` folder, so walking up from it never reaches the main checkout. Two layouts get past the new check and still fail the way this PR set out to prevent:

1. **A standalone package with its own lockfile.** This is the layout the PR targets. `linkEnvironment`'s doc says such a package "resolves from its own directory". `resolvesAbove` matches by name only, so a never-installed `tools/x` with `pnpm-lock.yaml` whose devDependencies (say `vitest`, `typescript`) are also root deps is not refused. `pnpm run` in a non-workspace package puts only the package's own `node_modules/.bin` on PATH, so the stage fails with `vitest: not found` (medium: pnpm internals). In this repo, `tools/review` is one dependency away from this: every dependency it declares except `zod` is also a direct root dependency.
2. **A dependency in an intermediate folder.** Take `tools/` as an installed yarn workspace root with `tools/review` as a member. `touchedNestedPackages` gives each file to the innermost package only (`typescript.adapter.ts:566-570`), so `tools/node_modules` is never linked. Yet `resolvesAbove` returns true at `rel = 'tools'`.

The function's own JSDoc says "the gate links the root's", so it means to count only the root. Neither layout has a test.

**Suggested direction:** count only the root (`rel === '.'`), and skip the hoisting allowance entirely when `pkg.dir` holds its own lockfile (`pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `package-lock.json`). Only workspace members hoist, and a member has no lockfile of its own.

findings.description: The install command in the refusal comes from `packageManager(<repo>/<pkg.dir>)`, which only looks for a lockfile in the package's own folder. Every yarn or pnpm workspace member therefore gets told to run `npm --prefix <dir> install`, which is the wrong tool and the wrong folder.
findings.body:
**A refused workspace member is told to install with npm in the member folder.**

```ts
const flag = INSTALL_DIR_FLAG[command.command] ?? '--prefix';
... `Install it with \`${shellWord(command.command)} ${flag} ${shellWord(dir)} install\`` ...
```

`command.command` is set by `packageManager(join(ctx.configPath, dir))` (`src/adapters/typescript.adapter.ts:170-174`, used at 578/586). That function only looks for `pnpm-lock.yaml` or `yarn.lock` in the member's own folder and otherwise returns `'npm'`. A workspace member keeps its lockfile at the workspace root, so every pnpm or yarn-v1 member resolves to `npm`. That was harmless while the value only ran `npm run <stage>`. This PR is the first to turn it into install advice.

**Trigger:** a pnpm or yarn workspace gains a member whose dependencies have not been installed in the main checkout yet, for example a new member added since the last `pnpm install`. The member has no `node_modules`, and `resolvesAbove` finds nothing at the root, because pnpm keeps member dependencies under `.pnpm` (medium: pnpm hoisting defaults). The gate then says "Install it with `npm --prefix tools/review install`":

- **pnpm:** npm rejects `workspace:` dependency specifiers, so the command fails.
- **yarn v1:** it writes a stray `package-lock.json` and an npm-built `node_modules` into the member, in the trusted checkout. That folder then satisfies the `existsSync(join(repoPath, pkg.dir, 'node_modules'))` early return, so later gate runs pass on an environment the repo doesn't use.

The per-manager `INSTALL_DIR_FLAG` table shows the message was meant to name the right tool. Its `yarn` and `pnpm` entries are only ever reached by standalone packages, and no test covers a refused workspace member.

**Suggested direction:** find the lockfile by walking up from `pkg.dir` to the root, and have the advice name that tool and that folder.

findings.description: ADR 0059's Ceilings paragraph still says an uninstalled nested package "fails its stage". The gate now refuses before any stage runs and names an install command, so the paragraph needs a one-line pointer to the new refusal.
The added sentence "A package with no environment to link is refused before anything is linked." restates the next line and `refuseUninstalled`'s JSDoc. Drop it.
